frontier_question: Why did Anthropic release Claude 4 as two models in May 2025, and what did the launch signal about the agentic-coding market?

chunks.content: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4 on 2025-05-08 — the "Claude 4" family: Opus 4 the flagship ("Claude 4"), Sonnet 4 the fast workhorse. Pricing: Opus 4 at $15 / $75 per million tokens (input/output), Sonnet 4 at $3 / $15 — Sonnet priced as the developer-default coding model. The headline capability was agentic coding and computer use: Claude 4's "computer use 2.0" (browser control) was roughly twice as reliable as the 3.x generation's, and the launch was timed to the rise of Claude Code as the defining agentic-coding product of 2025. The 4.1 update (2025-06-18) improved coding and agentic reliability at the same prices; the naming ("4.1" rather than "4.5") followed a reported internal dispute about Anthropic's version-naming policy. The direct competitive context was the OpenAI o-series and the enterprise agentic-coding gold rush; Anthropic positioned Claude 4 as the safest and most reliable coding agent and reported record API usage. Driven by Claude Code adoption, Anthropic raised a large funding round in late September 2025 at a reported ~$183 billion valuation, cementing its position as the coding-agent leader.

prior_gap_texts: Anthropic released the Claude 4 family, consisting of two models—Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4—on May 8, 2025 [Source: ev-1].

This dual-model strategy allowed Anthropic to position Opus 4 as its flagship model while designating Sonnet 4 as a faster "workhorse" priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, establishing it as the developer-default coding model [Source: ev-1].
In contrast, Opus 4 was priced higher at $15 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].
The launch signaled that agentic coding had become a defining market trend in 2025, with Claude Code emerging as the key product driving this shift [Source: ev-1].

By highlighting capabilities such as "computer use 2.0," which offered browser control roughly twice as reliable as previous generations, Anthropic positioned itself against competitors like OpenAI’s o-series during an enterprise agentic-coding gold rush [Source: ev-1].

The company aimed to establish Claude 4 as the safest and most reliable coding agent, a strategy that contributed to record API usage and ultimately supported a large funding round later in September 2025 at a reported valuation of approximately $183 billion [Source: ev-1].
